intro: One Loopforge console, six material directions. Compare the glass, hardware, supervisor sockets and control shapes. We can choose a whole direction or prototype a considered combination before building the production kit.

styles.name: Factory Original
styles.inspiration: Loopforge character sheets + original sim-sim chrome
styles.summary: Soot-dark enamel, aged brass and broad black glass. The starting sheet you responded to.
styles.strength: Closest to the existing factory and landing. Familiar material language with strong red/cyan character contrast.
styles.watch: Keep the worn detail subordinate to live text; reduce hardware around a six-screen wall.
styles.alt: Original Loopforge style study with black steel monitor, handwritten tape, brass fittings, circular supervisor tokens and a red control.

styles.name: Field Instrument
styles.summary: Olive enamel, bakelite grips, phosphor and a guarded mechanical lever. A console carried into service and repaired for years.
styles.strength: Clear selectors and substantial controls. The field-equipment silhouette gives the interface a distinct identity.
styles.watch: Keep Loopforge's full-colour characters. Do not import Fallout mascots, branding, green-only portraits or unused diagnostic modes.
styles.alt: Field Instrument style study with olive portable monitor, rubber grips, tape labels, square intercom portraits and hinged control lever.

styles.name: Broadcast Desk
styles.summary: Black ribbed housings, ivory keys and cartridge-like portrait sockets. More camera operator than machine engineer.
styles.strength: The clearest natural fit for six feeds and switching between a factory overview and focused conversations.
styles.watch: Ivory keys and pictograms can become too bright. A wrench must not suggest an available repair action before Witch arrives.
styles.alt: Broadcast Desk style study with dark ribbed camera monitor, ivory controls, rectangular character cartridges and blank dialogue balloons.

styles.name: Foundry Switchboard
styles.inspiration: Heavy industrial switchgear and foundry controls
styles.summary: Deep cast iron, protective rails, porcelain insulation and copper contacts. Every action feels like engaging factory machinery.
styles.strength: The strongest connection to the conveyor's weight, impact and mechanical sound language.
styles.watch: The substantial chassis consumes space. It needs a restrained six-camera arrangement, especially on phones.
styles.alt: Foundry Switchboard style study with heavy iron monitor, rails, copper contacts, U-shaped supervisor cradles and a rubber actuator.

styles.name: Submarine Watch
styles.inspiration: Naval control rooms and sealed optical instruments
styles.summary: Smoke-blue enamel, rubbed brass and deep curved glass. An enclosed observation post watching dangerous machinery.
styles.strength: Convincing glass depth and intercom hardware; a strong atmosphere for watching and interpreting events.
styles.watch: Capsule frames could overpower the camera feeds. Correct the generated LIMÉN caption and extinguish every status lamp on closed rooms.
styles.alt: Submarine Watch style study with blue sealed monitor, curved black glass, brass intercom portraits and a ceramic rotary control.

styles.name: Neural Diagnostics
styles.inspiration: Industrial medical equipment and Loopforge's brain machinery
styles.summary: Cracked ivory enamel over black steel, oxidized copper and cold cyan. The factory's clinical side, still dirty and physical.
styles.strength: Connects the interface to brain manufacturing and later cognitive inspection without changing the characters' identities.
styles.watch: Dense cracks can become visual noise. Reserve pale surfaces for important controls and never imply access to hidden psychology with decorative gauges.
styles.alt: Neural Diagnostics style study with worn ivory monitor casing, black glass, copper seams, cyan light and ceramic supervisor sockets.
